title: [epic] DID author verification — complete X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig
description:
Why: The DID author signature passthrough is already stubbed in the codebase (crates/reader/src/post/did_passthrough.rs, X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig header). The stub preserves the header through the pipeline but does not verify it. Completing this gives articles cryptographically verifiable authorship independent of the operator: an author signs their article with their own DID key before submission; any reader can verify the signature without trusting the operator.

What:
- Implement DID key resolution: support did:key (self-contained, no network lookup) and did:web (resolve via HTTPS) as a minimum.
- In the POST/IHAVE/TAKETHIS pipeline, if X-Usenet-IPFS-DID-Sig is present: resolve the DID, extract the verifying key, verify the signature over the article bytes.
- Verification result stored as a flag in the articles table (did_sig_valid: bool|null).
- Expose verification status in NNTP ARTICLE response headers, JMAP Email properties, and IMAP FETCH items.
- Invalid DID signatures: log a warning but do not reject the article (the operator signature is the trust anchor; DID sig is author self-attestation).
- Document the signing format so third-party clients can produce compliant headers.
notes: Review converged after 2 rounds. Final review: stoa-7537a275.
